questions.question: should I treat my boots out of box ? Annnnd how often should I treat them ?

hybrid.answer:
**Short version:** it depends on the boot, and I don't use a fixed schedule. As of 2022, I treat mine when they look or feel like they need it.

**Out of the box**
- Check the boot first. I looked at Blundstone's FAQ, which says most of their boots are pretreated and that they do not recommend treating them out of the box [1].
- Rustic Brown, Crazy Horse and rustic black styles are the exception. Per the FAQ, they "do not carry the same pretreatments as a finished and oiled leather" [2].
- I recommend conditioning those distressed boots rather than leaving them dry [3].
- In my first Blundstone review (2019) I said my distressed pair was water resistant. I later corrected that: "it looks like that is wrong" [4]. Once you have treated them, expect them to darken [5].

**How often**
- In 2022 I said: "really just use your intuition" [6]. I also admitted I "probably do too little" and treat them when I feel they need it [7].
- Treat them if the leather looks dry, feels dry, or no longer beads water. Wax if it isn't beading, and use oil if it looks dry [8].
- Clean your boots regularly, because dirt wears the leather down faster [9].
- In 2019 I was more specific: you may have to wax "every month maybe every week" if you go super crazy with your boots [10]. By 2022 I had dropped that schedule.
- If leather hasn't been conditioned in a few months, I'd condition it [11].

**Order of steps:** clean, then condition, then wax [12].

I've mostly covered Blundstones and leather boots in general. I haven't covered other boot constructions or finishes.

questions.question: So if I buy the levis 501 shrink to fit will they get tighter after washing?

hybrid.answer:
Yes, they get tighter, but mostly the first time you soak or wash them. After that, the waist loosens again with wear. They're unsanforized, so I'd size up before buying.

**Shrinking:** In my 2025 ranking I said you put them in the bathtub and "it'll shrink" [1]. In my 2023 vintage comparison I said unsanforized jeans "will shrink up to 10% when you wash them for the first time" [2]. When I shrank my own pair in 2019, the waist got very tight, while the length barely changed [3].

**Heat and dryer:** In my 2023 Wrangler comparison, the shrunk STFs got smaller than regular rinsed 501s [4]. The result depends on how you wash them. I didn't use very hot water or the dryer and they looked way better, so "don't toss your stfs in the dryer or rinse them that hot and you can get a really nice fit" [5].

**Stretching back out:** A week after shrinking mine, the waist and upper thigh had "definitely stretched" and I could wear a belt [6]. In 2023 I also said that if you wear them frequently, I bet they would "stretch out to about the same size" as the rinsed pair [7].

**Sizing:** My rule is to go two sizes up in the waist and two inches longer, as Levi's recommends [8][9]. I once bought my usual waist, a 29, and I could barely pull them on and couldn't breathe [10]. I'd also have gotten a longer length, a 32 [11].

I haven't covered how much they change over repeated washes after that first shrink.

questions.question: I'm usually a 33x30 in Levi's 502s, what size should I buy in these? [501 STF]

hybrid.answer:
I'd buy a 35 waist and a 32 length. That's my rule applied to your numbers: size up two in the waist and two inches in length. I haven't covered how the 502 fits compared with the 501, so I can't adjust for that.

**The rule (most recent first)**
- In 2025 I said of the shrink-to-fit 501: "You should usually go two sizes up." [1]
- In 2021 I explained that Levi's recommends going "two sizes bigger in the waist and then two inches longer than you would normally wear". It took me four pairs of 501s to learn Levi's is right. [2] After the soak, "your pants will fit regularly". [2]
- My example was that if you usually wear a 34, you get a 36. I added that I don't think a 36 exists, so you can be stuck. [3] I can't say whether a 35 waist is made, since I haven't covered odd sizes.

**Why waist +2**
- In 2023 I compared a size 30 rinsed pair with two size 32 STFs. The waist doesn't line up with vanity sizing, which is why you size up two in Levi's: it shrinks down. [4]

**Length**
- I bought a 30 length and said I definitely should have gotten a 32. [5] That matches the two inches longer rule, so 30 becomes 32 for you.

**Shrinking**
- Don't use very hot water or the dryer. I didn't, and my STFs looked way better. [6]

I went against Levi's advice in my first pair (a 29 waist, 30 length). I could barely pull them on, though I was glad later because the fit ended up good for me. [5] I'd still follow the rule for your first pair.

questions.question: Why do you cuff your jeans?

hybrid.answer:
Mostly it's about fixing length and avoiding wide, bunched-up legs. In my most recent video on this (2021), cuffing is my stopgap for not being able to settle on a hem length. By late 2019, though, I'd already started preferring jeans worn over my boots instead of cuffed.

**2021:** I can never decide between no break, half break or full break, so every pair feels like the wrong length [1]. The only solution I'd found, short of settling on one specific fit, was cuffing [2]. I also think the wider your pants, the higher the hem should be [3]. I do note that cuffs make your legs look shorter [4].

**2020:** I cuffed my Levi's 501s because I don't think my current style lends itself to uncuffed wider-legged pants [5]. I also said I should have bought them in a 32 length [5].

**Late 2019:** I said I always used to cuff my jeans, but now I like them over my boots a little more [6].

**Mid 2019:** Length matters most to me. If jeans look too long they just look bad, and a cuff can't be too thick [7].

questions.question: So do you prefer [the Red Wing 3335s] over the 1907s?

hybrid.answer:
**Yes, in 2022 I preferred the 3335s over the 1907s, but by September 2023 I'd hedged on that and was selling them.**

**Most recent view (2023):** I said I'm on record calling the 3335s my favorite Red Wings of all time, and that "they still might be but they probably not" [1]. I said the 875s, the 1907s and the Iron Rangers each have characteristics I really like [1]. I liked the 3335s for their stitch-down construction, lighter weight, and nimbleness for walking or a light hike [1]. I was still letting them go [2].

**2022 view:** I called the 3335s my favorite boots I've ever had, and said they beat my Blundstones, the 1907s and the 875s [3]. My reasoning:
- I'm going for hikes and walking in the woods rather than doing heritage work, so to me they're a dramatically better all-around boot [4].
- The 1907s and 875s are more beefily constructed, so if you need a tough boot, the 3335s are probably not the ones to go for [4].
- I prefer their Vibram mini lug sole to the crepe soles on the 875s and 1907s, since I don't think it will break down as fast [5].

**The 1907 case:** In 2021 I said that if you're looking at a moc toe Red Wing, I think you should get the 1907s [6].

questions.question: How do you feel bout blunnies as of Late 2023?

hybrid.answer:
As of my last word on them in September 2023, I'm still a big fan of Blundstones. I'm retiring my own pair, but that isn't a verdict against the boot.

**September 2023**
- On my first pair, the 585s, I said "bluntstones are just incredible I'm a big fan of them I've always loved them" [1].
- After heavy wear they "remained probably my most water resistant boots through it all" [2].
- I did say "I think it's time to retire those bunnies" [3]. That is part of cutting down my boot collection.
- I also noted that "some people seem to really not like them" [4].

**June 2022**
- I wrote "All in all I love Blundstones! Not as repairable as good year welted boots like Red Wings, or Wolverines but still some of my favorites." [5]

**August 2020, after one year**
- I was more measured. For work use, "it's decent for work boots but not anything incredible" [6].
- If I bought them again, I "would have gotten a smoother leather" instead of the rustic nubuck [7].

**May 2019, first impressions**
- Of the three or four boots I had, they were "by far my favorites" [8].

**Overall:** I like them more and more with time. The caveats I've raised are that they aren't easily resoled, that they aren't a standout work boot, and that I'd choose a smoother leather over the rustic one.

questions.question: I'm wondering if you still have these boots and how are they holding up??? [Blundstones]

hybrid.answer:
As of my September 2023 video, I was retiring my Blundstone 585s, so I can't say I still have them today. They had held up well, and I haven't covered anything about them since.

**2023 (most recent):** These are the 585s from my first-ever video. I said "you can see I've worn them constantly since I got them the leather is all beat up it's super shiny there's old wax conditioner whatever it may be they've held up through it all" [1]. They stayed "probably my most water resistant boots through it all" [1]. I still said "I think it's time to retire those bunnies" [1].

**2022:** After about two years of wearing them from the first cold days until mid-spring [2], I cleaned them, conditioned them with salve and oil, and waxed them. That was to restore the cracked dry leather [3].

**2020, after one year:** I said they looked great. The elastics were "a little looser than when i first got them", but still tight [4]. I also found some wear inside, at the big toe [5]. I still thought they were performing as I'd hoped for the price [6].

**Compared with other boots:** In 2022 I said my Red Wing 3335s beat my Blundstones as my favorite boots [7].

questions.question: How does the made in England boot stack up to Solovairs? [Dr. Martens]

hybrid.answer:
I think Solovair is the better boot, and I'd pick it over the Made in England Dr. Martens unless you specifically want the Dr. Martens look. My view has been the same from 2022 through 2023.

**Latest (Sept 2023):** Even after the quality problems with my pair, I said "through all of that I really like these boots" [1]. The fit felt loose, which I put down to sizing, and I'd sell them "only to get another pair of monkey boots" [1].

**Overall (May 2023):** I put it plainly: "the answer is Sol of a is better and Doc Martins is worse" [2]. With Solovair you get "a better boot that costs less with no artificial doc Martins markup" [3].

**Why I lean Solovair:**
- **Price:** In 2022 I said Solovair boots are "actually cheaper than doc martin made in england" [4]. In 2023 I put the gap at about $40 [3].
- **Midsole and outsole:** Solovair gives you "thicker heavier more robust felted midsoles" [5]. The outsole is also heavier and a little thicker [6].
- **Comfort:** In 2022 I said Solovair boots have a shank, "so they're a bit more comfortable over long periods of time" [7]. Dr. Martens have none [8].
- **Repair:** Solovair has its soles "available on their website" [9]. With Dr. Martens you're "basically out of luck" when you need new soles [10]. That is why I said Solovairs have a much longer lifespan [11].

**Downsides of Solovair:**
- **Quality control:** On my first pair, "the back tab on the back of one of the boots ripped off immediately" within a week in Denmark [12]. I thought that was a lemon. The eyelets still make me think the laces could wear out, which is "my only gripe with solar" [13].
- **Sizing:** My pair of Solovairs came up too big, so I'd size down half a size [14].

**When I'd still go Dr. Martens:** If the yellow stitching matters to you, you have to get the Made in England Dr. Martens [15]. When I compared them with the cheaper Thailand pair, I said the Made in England boots are for big fans: "right now you have to be a mega fan to get them" [16].

questions.question: Hi, I am going on a 4 day hike and I am wondering if I can use my blundstone for them, what do you think?

hybrid.answer:
I wouldn't pick Blundstones for a 4-day hike, though I haven't tested them on anything that long. The closest thing I've done is day hikes and mountain trips in Maine. They held up on those, but I called them poor mountain boots.

**Ankle support:** I did a few mountains in Maine in mine. I said "these are not good boots for mountaining apparently because they don't have uh good ankle support" [1]. They still "held up well" and only got scuffed [1]. With a pack over several days, that lack of ankle support is the thing I'd think hardest about.

**Comfort and blisters:** When I first got them I walked around the city and the woods and had no blisters [2]. Later I got break-in blisters when I started running and walking the track in them, and those stopped after two to three weeks [3]. So I'd make sure they're fully broken in before a long trip.

**Water:** After a year untreated, I stood in a pond and my feet stayed dry apart from a little water at the elastic band. That makes them fine for crossing a brook or standing in mud [4]. If you want them water resistant, keep them treated. I'd say untreated or old leather that needs retreating "is not hydrophobic" [5].

**Overall:** I think of them as decent for work but not incredible [6]. They suit casual everyday use more than serious trail days.

If you want the closest thing I've said about long hikes, I keep my Jim Green Razorbacks partly because they have "a lot of padding so if you're going hiking for a long time that's good stuff" [7]. I haven't compared them to Blundstones directly, and I haven't covered multi-day hiking in the Blundstones themselves.

questions.question: I'm 5'11-225 lbs with a dad bod. What's the most cost efficient and quality t shirt for me? Also, what size would u prefer?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** For cost and quality together, I'd point you to Uniqlo, or Muji if you need more length and width. I haven't given a specific size for 5'11" and 225 lbs, so I can't name one.

**Best value:** As of my September 2025 video, a $20 Uniqlo tee is "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price." [1] Earlier in 2025 I said that for $15 you get a bound neck collar that doesn't wiggle, and that I wear the black one all the time. [2]

**Why Muji might suit you better:** I said Uniqlo is the starter tee "unless if you're taller or wider in any way, shape, or form, you'd want Muji." [3] It costs about $4 or $5 more but is significantly longer and a good deal wider. [3] You're at 225 lbs, so by that rule Muji is the one I'd point you to.

**If you'll spend a bit more:** House of Blanks is $35, made in Canada, and had zero torque (no twisting after washing). I called it an outstanding value. [4]

**Size:** I don't have a rule for your measurements. These are the closest things I've said:
- In a tee I like a lot of space across the shoulders. [5]
- The Los Angeles Apparel tee fits large, and I said it might win if you size down one. [6]
- Brands run differently, so size by brand.

questions.question: Am I the only one who loves these videos but in the end still has no idea which to buy? Please just tell me: buy this one, or these 3. I can't decide between 25 options. [t-shirts]

hybrid.answer:
I don't name one single best t-shirt, and my most recent t-shirt video (September 2025) explains why. If you want a shortcut, here are three of my picks at different spending levels.

**Why there's no single answer:** I said that 99.999% of people can make a really good t-shirt now, and that it "just has to line up with your preferences to be the best t-shirt" [1]. The best I can do is describe the shirts and how they feel, and you decide what you want [2].

**Three picks from my winner circle:**
- **Cheapest:** Uniqlo. At $20, it's probably the best t-shirt you can get "bar none for the price" [3]. It's open-end and a bit rough, and I call it your starter t-shirt [4].
- **Mid-range all-arounder:** J. Press x American Trench. I was torn between it and 3Sixteen, but I went with J. Press for its rougher hand feel [5].
- **Clean, modern, more expensive:** Merz b. Schwanen 2M15. In the Supremes category, "for some reason today" I felt it edged out Lady White [6].

**Other picks by category:**
- Japanese tees: I'd give it to Wonder Looper for its much more universal fit [7].
- Heavyweights: American Giant, by a long shot [8].
- Best value, character vs. smoothness: choose Front General Store if you like more character, or House of Blanks if you want perfectly smooth with no torque. Today I'm feeling the Front General Store [9].

**How my views have shifted:** In 2024, Asket won my t-shirt competition [10]. In 2025 I said it's "still very very high up there" [11], but I leaned toward Merz b. Schwanen in that category. In a June 2025 value ranking, I put Bronson and Bravestar slightly above Uniqlo [12]. I also said the Los Angeles Apparel tee might win if you size down one [13]. Because I list many winners rather than one, these are the closest I get to a short list.

questions.question: 1907 vs the 875's? What's the difference?

hybrid.answer:
**Short version:** in my 2021 video I said I'd pick the 1907 over the 875 if you're looking at a Red Wing moc toe. Later videos don't change that. In 2023 I said the 875s, 1907s and Iron Rangers all have characteristics I really like [1].

**What's different**
- **Welt:** The 875 is Goodyear welted. I call Goodyear welts durable and pretty water resistant [2]. The 1907 has the storm welt. From what I found on Reddit, Red Wing's version isn't that complex: they stitch another strip of leather onto the welt [3]. I said the storm welt is invaluable to me [4].
- **Extras:** The 1907 comes with Red Wing's removable leather footbed, which typically costs $40 separately. It also comes with leather laces, which are typically $15 [4].
- **Price:** The 1907 is $10 more than the 875, but I argue that works out to a better deal because of those extras [5].

**Shared traits:** Both have crepe soles, which I don't really like [6]. I also called both of them more beefily constructed than the 3335s, so they suit you better if you need a tough boot [7].

**Water resistance:** In my waterproof test, the right 1907 leaked almost immediately through the stitching, but the left stayed dry. I still think they'd hold up fine in rain, grass or mud [8]. I wear them a lot day to day, but leather welted boots don't do a ton for me functionally when it's wet [9].

**My pick:** I still highly recommend the 1907s [9]. I haven't made a direct side-by-side comparison of fit or break-in between the 1907 and the 875.

questions.question: How does Uniqlo compare to The Front General Store,  Proclub, and Hanes? ie what is the best budget shirt?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** Uniqlo is the best budget shirt for most people. Front General Store is the better pick if you want a Japan-made shirt with more character and can spend about $40. I haven't compared all four side by side in one video, so this combines my separate reviews.

**Uniqlo (my most recent view, 2025):** At $20 it is "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" [1]. I call it a starter shirt: open-end yarn and a bit rough [2]. Earlier that year I said that for $15 you get a bound neck collar so it doesn't wiggle, and that you could end the video there [3]. In 2024 I also named the Uniqlo heavyweight crew neck the best value heavyweight or all-around tee [4]. If you're taller or wider, I'd look at Muji instead of Uniqlo [5].

**Front General Store:** It's a $40, 100% made-in-Japan shirt with great proportions and a great feel [6]. I called it "still really good" at about $38 [7]. In 2024 I gave it a softness of 6 out of 10 [8]. Of the two best-value picks, I said that if you like a lot of character, you have to go Front General Store, and that on that day I was feeling it [9].

**Pro Club:** I like it overall, although I said it was the roughest shirt in that video, with a softness of 4 out of 10 [10]. It's a worthwhile budget option, but it's not the softest.

**Hanes:** I called it "your classic $10 great shirt" with a softness of 7 out of 10 [11]. It shrank 6.73% in length in my test, so I'd expect it to get shorter after washing [11].

**My lean:** Uniqlo for the best price-to-quality ratio. Front General Store if you want Japan-made character. Hanes if you want the cheapest decent shirt. Pro Club is a fine rough, old-school shirt but not a standout. I also said the best tee comes down to your own preferences [12].

questions.question: Would you recommend this [Barbour Bedale] or the flint and tinder for someone who would use it like a rain jacket but also a windbreaker and a spring light jacket?

hybrid.answer:
**I'd lean toward the Bedale for what you describe, though I haven't tested the Flint and Tinder as a rain jacket.** Nothing in my videos compares the two for rain, wind and spring wear head to head, so this is my read from what I've said about each.

**Barbour Bedale**
- In my 2025 ranking I said a Barbour isn't a designated rain jacket, since I take that to mean lightweight fabric, and it's the lightest fabric in the ranking [1]. Because of that, "any time of year, you could toss on your Barber and be super comfortable" [2]. That fits your spring-jacket use.
- For rain, it has features aimed at it: storm cuffs that help in bad weather [3], and a storm flap over the zipper so water won't run through it [4]. I also suggest getting the hood [5].
- In my shower test a new Bedale didn't leak at all, but that was with a brand-new coat of wax and oil [6]. How water-resistant it is depends on the state of the wax. As it ages and patinas you lose a bit of practicality, and I might be in the camp that minds that [7].
- I haven't said anything specific about the Bedale as a windbreaker.

**Flint and Tinder Waxed Trucker**
- In 2025 I said it's built for everyone: not crazy lightweight, but lighter weight and comfortable [8]. I also said the $300 price for a lined, US-made jacket makes it hard not to recommend [9]. That segment was sponsored by Huckberry, though I said I'd talked about the jacket many times before the sponsorship [10].
- I'm less sure of this one. In 2023 I said it was for a specific man that is not me, though I'd love it slightly modified [11].
- I haven't tested its rain resistance or wind resistance in my videos.

**My pick:** the Bedale, because I've actually tested its rain performance and it has the rain-specific details. The Flint and Tinder is a comfortable, well-priced lined jacket if you'd rather not spend more on the Barbour.

questions.question: Great video. But just curious, how can you say it's a con that the Huckberry jacket is unlined when they sell two different versions of lined waxed truckers: wool, and flannel?

hybrid.answer:
You're right that Huckberry sells lined versions. The con only applied to the unlined one I had in my 2023 comparison. The lined flannel version I've praised, and the wool-lined one I haven't tried yet.

**The 2023 comparison (September 2023).** The Huckberry jacket in that video was "the cheapest most simple unlined basic jacket on this list" [1]. My con was about that version: "the one con that Rogue territory and huckberry have for me is that they are not lined. I personally always like aligning on wax jackets just so the wax isn't touching your clothes" [2]. I'd already said in 2022 that Huckberry offers an unlined option [3], and in April 2023 I pointed out there is a wool-lined version too [4].

**The lined version (May 2025).** When I covered the lined Flint and Tinder trucker, I said "It's lined, so that way it's comfortable. You don't get wax on your skin." I also said they make a wool-lined one "that I'm yet to get" [5]. That segment was sponsored by Huckberry, though I said I'd talked about this jacket many times before they sponsored me [6].

**My view on unlined jackets has softened.** In 2025, talking about the unlined Rogue Territory jacket, I said that usually I want a liner on a wax jacket because the wax gets on your skin, but "in my old age... I kind of see why you wouldn't line something" [7]. I'd still call lining a con on the unlined Huckberry, but it matters less to me than it used to.

questions.question: Do you know how these fit compared to the 875s? [Red Wing 3335s]

hybrid.answer:
I haven't directly compared the fit of the 3335s and the 875s in my videos, so I can't say how they differ side by side. Here is what I did say about the 3335s, plus the closest thing I covered on the other Red Wings.

**3335s:** I went true to size and they fit fine. [1] The profile is slim and tapered, with a very thin outsole. [1] With thin cotton socks in warm weather I had no tightness. With wool socks my toes feel squished and I can't wiggle them much. [1]

**The 875s:** I haven't given a sizing note for them. I only said the 1907s and 875s are more beefily constructed than the 3335s. [2] That is about build, not fit.

**Closest thing I covered:** for the 1907s, I usually wear an 8 in boots, bought an 8 in Red Wings, and they fit perfectly. [3] My general Red Wing advice is to buy them snug but not squished. [3] That was about the 1907s, not the 875s.
